posts.title_en: Scale42 CEO: 'I'd rather build in Kristinestad than Texas'
posts.alt: Kristinestad, Finland - coastal site in the wind-power heartland
posts.excerpt_en: Vasabladet on Scale42's plan to develop a hyperscale data centre on the wind-rich Ostrobothnian coast.
posts.excerpt_no: Vasabladet om Scale42s plan om et hyperskala datasenter på den vindrike Österbottenskysten.
posts.subtitle: A 235-hectare hyperscale-grade site, four 400 kV substations and a top-five Finnish municipality for wind-power generation.
posts.tags: Kristinestad, Finland, Ostrobothnia, Wind power, Vasabladet
posts.source_html: As reported by Vasabladet and developer Redeve Oy.
posts.body_html:
In an interview with Swedish-language daily Vasabladet, Scale42 CEO William Tasney explained why his next major AI data centre is heading to coastal Ostrobothnia rather than the data centre belts of the United States.

The Kristinestad site, developed by Redeve Oy in partnership with the City of Kristinestad, reserves 235 hectares for hyperscale-grade data centre development. The area sits at the heart of Finland’s wind-power production — Kristinestad ranks in the country’s top five municipalities by wind energy output — with four 400 kV substations and Fingrid’s main grid backbone serving Western Finland.

Scale42’s planned investment, according to Vasabladet, exceeds the €1 billion commitment TikTok publicly announced for its own Finnish data centre project, making it one of the largest privately backed digital infrastructure projects in the country.

"I would rather build here than in Texas." — William Tasney, CEO, Scale42

The rationale, in Tasney’s view, comes down to four factors:

  • Wind-dominant electricity at some of the lowest wholesale prices in Europe
  • Grid headroom — four 400 kV substations and adjacent solar zones in development
  • Logistics via the 15-metre-deep shipway into Karhusaari harbour for heavy equipment
  • Stakeholder alignment — a municipality that has spent years preparing land and zoning for industrial-scale digital infrastructure

An advance reservation agreement was signed on 11 February 2025, with zoning and joint customer development now progressing alongside the City of Kristinestad.

"We are currently developing new data centre operations jointly with the city and customers." — Timo Heiskanen, CEO, Redeve Oy
"Kristinestad has attained an edge by identifying the future needs of industry." — Lauri Koskinen, Zoning Manager, City of Kristinestad

For Scale42, Kristinestad anchors the company’s Finnish footprint alongside its earlier projects in Varkaus and Kitee — a portfolio targeting low-cost, low-carbon AI compute at industrial scale on land that already has the power and connectivity to support it.

posts.title_en: Scale42 plans AI data centre in Kitee, Finland
posts.title_no: Scale42 planlegger KI-datasenter i Kitee, Finland
posts.alt: Kitee, Finland - Puhos industrial area site for the Scale42 data centre
posts.excerpt_en: Data Centre Dynamics on Scale42's 10-hectare Puhos site, with 10 MW available now scaling to 200 MW.
posts.excerpt_no: Data Centre Dynamics om Scale42s 10-hektar Puhos-tomt, med 10 MW tilgjengelig nå skalerbar til 200 MW.
posts.subtitle: 10-hectare Puhos industrial site offers 10 MW today and is scalable to 200 MW via the Fingrid national grid.
posts.tags: Kitee, Finland, North Karelia, Data Centre Dynamics
posts.source_html: As reported by Data Centre Dynamics and Business Joensuu.
posts.body_html:
Scale42 will develop a new AI-ready data centre in Kitee’s Puhos industrial area, eastern Finland. Construction is targeted for 2026, with operations beginning in 2027–28.

The City of Kitee has agreed to sign a Preliminary Real Estate Sale and Purchase Agreement with Scale42 for a 10-hectare plot in the northern part of the Puhos industrial area. The site offers 10 MW available today, with capacity scalable to 200 MW via connection to Fingrid’s national grid — one of the cleanest electricity mixes in Europe.

The project is expected to create 50–100 permanent jobs during operations, in addition to construction-phase employment. It marks the first industrial-scale data centre development in the North Karelia region.

"Kitee is a place with deep industrial roots and pride. We want to help be a part of its next chapter, diversifying into the digital economy." — William Tasney, CEO, Scale42

For Kitee, the project arrives as the municipality’s Puhos area transitions from its forest-industry heritage toward higher-value technology sectors.

"This project offers a huge boost to our region through the creation of new jobs." — Pekka Hirvonen, Mayor of Kitee

Business Joensuu, the regional development agency supporting the deal, framed it as an inflection point for the wider region.

"This project marks an exciting milestone as the first industrial-scale data centre development in the North Karelia region." — Pauliina Pikkujämsä, Director, Business Joensuu

Scale42’s selection of Kitee reflects the broader thesis behind its 1.7 GW Nordic pipeline: industrial sites with strong existing grid infrastructure, low-cost renewable electricity, and supportive local stakeholders — in regions where AI compute can be deployed responsibly and at scale.
